note: Human prompts are paraphrased from the real session for clarity. The participant's own wording, status checks and discussions about the log format are omitted at the participant's request, and environment-setup turns are condensed to one line. Every paraphrase is tied to the timestamp of the real message (the rebuild refuses entries without one, and fails if any fragment of a real human message remains). All agent actions, sub-agents, skills, tools, verification results and commits are recorded as they happened.

turns.prompt:
Analyse the assignment PDF and the reference repository. Produce a complete implementation and demo-video plan, then explain the assignment and plan simply. The agent does all implementation, testing and documentation; I only record the video and submit.

Working rules: verify every step from live output, log everything so work can resume after any interruption, re-check logs and live code before continuing, and never change git remotes or cloud resources yourself; give me the command instead.
turns.answer: Read the assignment PDF and every file of the reference repository, checked the toolchain (the .NET SDK was missing), and wrote the plan files: phases, the fourteen deliverables, a commit plan, a test matrix, decisions and a resumable worklog. Explained the assignment and the plan in short points.

turns.prompt:
Plan owners per stage: the agent completes everything; I handle only the restart, the push and pull request, and the video. Run independent work with parallel agents.

Generate the AI interaction log automatically through hooks: structured JSONL plus a readable summary, covering tool, model, agent type, mode, prompts, skills, sub-agents, MCP tools, actions, human decisions, evidence and outcome.
turns.answer: Re-planned with an owner for every step, parallel agents on disjoint file sets and a local run-and-test protocol; adopted the requested log schema (JSONL plus readable summary) and listed what the demo video must show live.

turns.prompt: Use Claude Code as the AI tool. No workshop review prompt is available, so write a structured review prompt of your own and state that in the write-up.
turns.answer: Recorded the decisions: Claude Code as the tool, our own structured review prompt, local commits by the agent with push and pull request done by the participant.

turns.prompt: Local commits by the agent are allowed; I push and open the pull request. Use the GitHub no-reply address as commit author, and clone from my fork.
turns.answer: Set the repository-local commit identity to the GitHub no-reply address, confirmed the clone of the fork, inspected the upstream demo branches read-only (they hold no review prompt) and moved the pull request before the video in the plan.

turns.prompt: Continue from the plan: capture the baseline and the mutation score before any change, then build the agent context in parallel (AGENTS.md, skills, sub-agents, hooks) and commit it.
turns.answer: Baseline: build clean, 7 tests green; Stryker before: 30.77 % overall, ApprovalService 60 %. Three parallel agents wrote AGENTS.md, the hooks and logger, and the skills and sub-agents; every file was reviewed, a privacy gap in the logger was fixed, and commit C1 was made.

turns.prompt: Prepare a submission-ready zip and confirm when everything is done.
turns.answer: Agreed: all remaining work, the pull-request description and a verified zip are produced by the agent; only the video remains afterwards.

turns.prompt: Order of delivery: finish all work, open the pull request with the review verdicts in its description, then submit the zip; the video comes last and its link is provided with the submission.
turns.answer: Recorded the delivery order: pull request with the review verdicts first, then the zip; the video and its link last.

turns.prompt: Complete the remaining work end to end: specification, step 1, step 2, end-to-end test, mutation testing, review and write-up. Use parallel agents where files do not overlap, verify everything, and work safely.
turns.answer: OpenSpec change written and strictly validated (C2). Step 1 and step 2 implemented by parallel implementer and test-author agents, each followed by an adversarial test review whose eight findings were fixed and proven with hand-applied mutants, plus API and UI checks (C3, C4). Playwright end-to-end test added and run from a clean start (C5). Mutation testing started.

turns.prompt: Pause at the next safe point.
Set the mutation-score target yourself, keeping the before and after comparison honest.
turns.answer: Target set: make Approve and LimitFor genuinely mutable, kill every non-equivalent mutant in the approval code, add clearly labelled tests for the untested DiscountCalculator and Invoice defaults, and keep the Stryker configuration identical to the before run.
